title: Minimax Risk for the Local Contrast of Two Minimum-Dose Policies
banked_reason: Sound proposal-level full-ray versus off-ray risk separation is incremental, below required field floor; final review has no soundness/structure flags but N-strawman, N-no-stat-frontier-advance, N-thin-survey remain unrepaired. Independent validity gate confirms exhausted authorized scope.
gap_reasons: The negative kernel names no published estimator, paper, or workflow using the tent-ray shortcut; the core itself says it “does not overturn a published ray-sufficiency theorem” and supplies no comparator bibkey.
A fixed Gaussian-risk separation for a self-defined ray has neither a rate/limit law/efficiency result nor a strict improvement or first bound for a named published causal estimator or estimand.

The statement-level survey omits closer Gaussian-white-noise functional literature, including Ibragimov--Has'minskii (1984/1985), Donoho--Liu (1991), and Zhao (1997), which must be distinguished from the proposed all-rule ray claim.
proof_attempt_summary: The original exact full-box risk/interval and Bernoulli-equivalence program failed its early-kill certificate requirement. One authorized seed-ray retry produced a complete-amplitude ray risk upper of 0.36362392569873203 and admissible off-ray prior Bayes enclosure [0.37572028697318194, 0.37616259349180625], with a robust narrow-separation extension; the final panel found no soundness or structure defect but assessed both headlines incremental. No Lean module was produced; a named published comparator, causal statistical frontier, and closest Gaussian-functional literature audit remain prerequisites for any future re-raise.
tldr: The complete opposite-tent amplitude ray has strictly smaller unrestricted squared-risk difficulty than the entire bounded unit-Lipschitz Gaussian parent for the local contrast of two exact minimum-dose policies. An explicit rule covers every ray amplitude, and an admissible four-signal prior supplies the parent lower bound. At unit multiplier and separation, replayable finite certificates give ray risk at most \(0.3637\), prior Bayes risk at least \(0.3757\), and a gap at least \(0.0120\). The gap persists for separations in \([0.999,1]\), every admissible window, and every positive multiplier. The posterior-risk sufficiency frontier at the remaining separations is open.
gap: Published line-segment reductions provide lower bounds, while convex Gaussian optimal-recovery results address specified affine or confidence criteria. The inherited sources do not identify the entire fixed tent ray with this unrestricted Lipschitz decision problem.
fill: Explicit ray and off-ray constructions yield a finite, continuum-valid separation certificate and its persistence under separation changes. The broader equality frontier remains an open decision question; the numerical instance alone does not establish a field-level advance.
